headline: Good blanks.

fields.
hero.lede: An independent review of royalapparel.net for the Digital Marketing & Ecommerce Coordinator role. I read the homepage, the sitemap's 1,063 URLs, the Men's category and 20 product pages — 39 page fetches plus 17 header checks, no logins, no carts. The garments are well documented: 28 colors, 9 sizes and 107 photos on style 5051. The data around them is not: no canonical on any page, a sitemap that is 38% redirects, a five-star rating hard-coded on every product, and GA4 events whose product names are empty strings. Six findings, five working fixes.

why.title: Why Royal Apparel
why.sub: Two new facilities, a West Coast warehouse and a new import division in twelve months means more styles, two inventory states and a second brand to keep straight in categories, feeds and tracking. That is the job in the posting.
rows: Category grid, sort order, $0.00 tiles, “New” on everything, Men = Unisex — finding 5.
Redirect chain, canonicals, the sitemap — findings 1 and 2.
Feeds for Google, Faire, Sage, ASI
One Product schema with real availability, brand and color — finding 3.
What the dataLayer sends today and what it should send — finding 4.
Size charts, alt text, news page, video — finding 6.
why.note: Everything here comes from public pages: served HTML, the sitemap, robots.txt and the inline product JSON the site itself uses to render. Nothing was submitted, carted or logged into. The platform is custom, so every fix is written at the template or web-server level rather than for a particular app.

strengths.title: Fresh, on-brand homepage merchandising
strengths.text: The four hero slides were produced within the last three weeks (files dated Sep 9–23, 2026), all four link to live pages, the carousel is ARIA-labelled, and the Women / Men / Heavyweight / Vintage Washed tiles carry descriptive alt text.

strengths.title: Unusually deep product data and imagery
strengths.text: Style 5051 ships 28 colors × 9 sizes (XS–5X) with 107 alt-view images and specific alts (“Unisex Short Sleeve Tee BLACK Back”); the 19 live sampled PDPs average about 73 words of real spec copy. Product URLs are self-healing — /product/5051/anything.html, /product/5051/ and the CGI form all 301 to the canonical slug.

strengths.title: Clear wholesale terms and a search that respects style numbers
strengths.text: Prices are public; /shipping states the rule precisely (free freight at $350 per warehouse, $9.95 handling, in-stock only, updated Oct 30, 2025); customer service lists phone, address, hours and the RA returns process. Searching “5051” returns the style in position 1.

findings.title: The homepage is a meta-refresh stub; four hostnames answer 200 and no page carries a canonical
findings.count: 4 of 4 host/protocol variants return 200 · 0 of 24 HTML pages with a canonical · lowercase /category/men/ also 200
findings.observed: https://www.royalapparel.net/ is a 515-byte file whose only content is a meta refresh to a CGI URL, which 301s to /index, where the real homepage lives — without a canonical. The stub is the one page on the site that has a canonical, and it points at itself. http://, https://, www and non-www all return byte-identical 200 responses; there is no redirect to one hostname (HSTS is sent, which browsers honour only after a first HTTPS visit). /Category/Men without the slash is a 404; /category/men/ in lowercase is a second live copy.
findings.why: The posting owns technical SEO and GEO. With no canonicals and four live hostnames, link equity and AI-crawler citations split across duplicates, and the homepage's own signals point at an empty stub.
findings.fix: At the web server: 301 http → https and non-www → www; serve the homepage at / and 301 /index to it (or the reverse — one of the two); delete the stub. In the layout template: a self-referencing canonical on every page built from the pretty path. Case-fold category paths and 301 the slash-less form.

findings.title: The sitemap is 38% redirects, lists checkout and login pages, and serves dead products as 200
findings.count: 408 of 1,063 URLs are redirecting CGI category links · 16 cart/login/checkout pages · 0 of 248 product URLs with lastmod · 3 of 20 sampled products dead or obsolete but 200
findings.observed: The sitemap robots.txt points to (on the non-www host) lists 1,063 URLs. 408 are CGI catalog_browse links that every one 301 to a pretty /Category/ URL — and the pretty targets are not in the file. Sixteen more are cart, abandoned-cart, checkout, login, password-reset and wish-list templates, plus /404 and a test page. No product URL has a lastmod; the newest date anywhere is 2024-07-23. Of 20 sampled products, /product/15250006/USA-Team-Beanie.html returns 200 with the body “Product Not Found,” and two more carry itemStatus “obsolete” while remaining listed and indexable.
findings.why: “Deactivate discontinued items” is the posting's first merchandising duty; a sitemap that spends 40% of its entries on redirects and lists the checkout tells Google the catalog is unmaintained.
findings.fix: Regenerate the sitemap nightly from the catalog: only www pretty URLs (/index, /Category/…/, /Accessory-Type/…/, /product/{style}/{slug}.html, landing pages) with a real lastmod per product; exclude obsolete items, Product-Not-Found styles and every CGI template; serve it on the www host and update robots.txt. Return 404 or 410 for retired styles and 301 obsolete styles to their replacement where the PDP already names one.

findings.title: Product schema is split in two, blank on availability, and carries the same 5★ / 326-review rating on every product
findings.count: 19 of 19 PDPs with two Product blocks · 19 of 19 with Offer.availability “” · 19 of 19 identical aggregateRating 5 / 326 · 0 of 20 BreadcrumbList, og:image, GTIN or MPN · 150 of 150 color hexes set to FFFFFF
findings.observed: Each product page emits one Product with an Offer whose url, priceValidUntil and availability are empty strings, a Corporation block with empty url and logo, and a second Product carrying brand “Royal Apparel” and aggregateRating 5 from 326 ratings — identical on a $6.44 beanie and a $33.45 hoody. The feed attributes Google Shopping and Faire need are only partly present: color and size exist in the inline product JSON, but every color's hexColor is the placeholder FFFFFF, availSizes is empty for all 28 colors, and brand, GTIN and per-variant availability appear nowhere in the HTML.
findings.why: The posting asks for feed optimization and marketplace product data. Google's product rich results need one Product with brand, offers.availability and an authentic rating; a sitewide fabricated review count is what gets Merchant Center listings disapproved.
findings.fix: In the product template, output one Product: name, sku/mpn (the style code), brand (Royal Apparel, or Basic Supply Co. when the mill code is BSC), the image array, plain-text description, an AggregateOffer from the low/high wholesale price with availability derived from the same quantity the page already uses, no aggregateRating unless it comes from real reviews, plus BreadcrumbList and og:image. Fill hexColor from the swatch palette and export GTIN per SKU in the feed.

findings.title: GA4 receives products without names, views without currency and no list attribution
findings.count: 21 of 21 category impressions with blank item_name and item_brand · 20 of 20 view_item pushes without currency or brand · page-level push array-wrapped on every template · 0 view_item_list or select_item events anywhere
findings.observed: GTM-TG38JDV loads on every page and the site declares enhancedEcomm true. The page-level push is dataLayer.push([{…}]) — the object is wrapped in an array, so pageType and pageID are not readable as Data Layer Variables. The Men's listing pushes 21 impressions with item_name “”, item_brand “” and price as a formatted string. The PDP's view_item uses value at item level instead of price, with no currency, item_brand or item_variant; related products are pushed in the Universal Analytics impressions shape with no event, so GA4 never gets a view_item_list. The add_to_cart code is written twice — once with currencyCode, once with currency.
findings.why: The posting says “validate GA4 and tag-manager tracking” and build the dashboards. With these payloads, item reports show IDs without names, revenue-less views and no attribution for the merchandising the coordinator is meant to optimize.
findings.fix: Change the page push to a plain object; emit view_item_list on listings with item_list_id, item_list_name and complete items (name from the description, brand from the mill code, numeric price, index) and select_item on click; send view_item with currency, value and item-level price, brand and variant; replace the UA-shaped related push with a second view_item_list; standardize add_to_cart on currency. Verify in GTM Preview and GA4 DebugView, then add a data-quality tile (name and price coverage) to the dashboard.

findings.title: Category grid: 21 of 136 Men's products in the HTML, $0.00 tiles, “New” on everything, Men = Unisex
findings.count: 21 of 136 products (15%) present in HTML · 3 of 21 tiles at $0.00 · 21 of 21 flagged new · position 1 is an imported tee · Men (136) = Unisex (136) · 90 of 359 images without alt
findings.observed: /Category/Men/ renders its grid client-side from an inline JSON blob; the served HTML contains one product link. Pages 2–7 are reached by setting a hash and reloading — no page links, no rel next/prev — so 115 of 136 products are not linked from any crawlable URL. Inside the 21: three custom garment-dye programs show $0.00 with no swatches; all 21 carry isNew true (the badge markup is commented out, so the flag means nothing); position 1 under “manual” sort is a $4.93 Basic Supply Co. import on a category whose hero says USA Manufacturer. Men and Unisex are the same 136 items under two URLs; Accessories still lives at the pandemic-era slug /Category/Face-Cover-Accessories/. Searching “5051” interleaves two imports at positions 2–3 ahead of the 5051 family.
findings.why: Tagged product groups, sort order, deactivating items and category curation are the core of the posting, and the data shows the levers are not being used.
findings.fix: Server-render the first page of cards with real pagination links and a canonical; give custom-dye programs a “Request pricing” tile instead of $0.00; reset isNew to a 60-day window from the street date; canonicalize Men to Unisex or curate a distinct Men's assortment; 301 the Face-Cover slug to /Category/Accessories/; pin Royal-made styles above Basic Supply Co. imports on USA-positioned categories and in style-number search.

findings.title: Size charts are images labelled “Pick your color”, no product video, a News page with no news, a footer link that 404s sitewide
findings.count: 18 chart images, 0 tables · 13 of 15 chart alts read “Pick your color” · 0 of 19 PDPs with video · 0 dated posts on /in-the-news · 1 footer link → 404 on every page · 38 of 38 image filenames are timestamps
findings.observed: The only size guidance is /product-specifications: 61 words of text and 18 images, no HTML table, no PDF; 13 of the 15 chart images carry alt text copied from a color page. No sampled PDP has a video, although the template supports one. The footer “News” link opens a 47-word intro with no articles, while the company's three real stories from the last year — the West Coast DC, the second Hauppauge plant, Basic Supply Co. — appear only on trade sites. “Eco-Certifications” in the footer returns 404 on every page, next to a stray “--->” from a broken comment. The homepage has no h1.
findings.why: An AI answer engine cannot read a size chart that is a JPEG labelled “Pick your color,” and a news page with no news undercuts the story the company is paying trade press to tell.
findings.fix: Rebuild the size charts as HTML tables (one per fit, inch and cm) and surface the matching table in the PDP Specs tab; fix the 13 alts. Publish the three 2025–26 stories on /in-the-news with dates and NewsArticle schema, then a monthly cadence from new-style drops. Point Eco-Certifications at a real page or remove it. Shoot short colorway clips for the top 20 styles and set the video fields the template already reads. Name new uploads by style and color.

also: The Corporation JSON-LD on every page has empty url and logo fields.
robots.txt correctly disallows search-result and preview URLs; the search page itself has no noindex, so the disallow is the only guard.
Three copies of jQuery load on every page (2.2.2, 3.3.1, and a broken entity-encoded path).
The related-products strip surfaces deep clearance beside core styles (a $6.00 toddler tee at $0.99) — 19 such rows across the 20 sampled PDPs; worth confirming those prices are intended.
store_locator.p is in the sitemap but renders the unconfigured “Store Locator Template.”
No skip link on any page; the UserWay widget is loaded instead.
